t: You're on Dawes Street, in Walworth, in the borough of Southwark. The street is named after James Dawes, an English solicitor and businessman who sat as a Liberal Member of Parliament from 1910 until 1921. He lived from 1866 to 1921, so he died while still holding his seat. Dawes is the person this ordinary Walworth street remembers, and there is a link between local streets and the politicians of his day.
